weapons.name: Cataclysm
weapons.note: Fast attacks with wide area effects. The consensus best pull in every tier list published so far — Zenless is the top rung and Cataclysm is the only weapon on it.

weapons.name: Cursed King
weapons.note: In-game card: “The undisputed King of Curses. Dominates the fight with high-speed slashes, massive area fire bursts, and total domain control.” Sits in S tier on the tier board circulating in creator videos.

weapons.name: Shanks
weapons.note: Mythic sword fighter built around heavy energy slashes. Ranks at the top of the Mythic band in the tier lists checked.

weapons.name: Alucard
weapons.note: Ranged weapon with combo attacks. A healing effect is claimed by some showcases and is not confirmed by any published source — treat it as unverified.

weapons.name: Lights of Divinity
weapons.note: Golden slashes and pillars of light that hit a wide area. Mythic band, area-damage role.

weapons.name: Kings Gambit
weapons.note: In-game card: “The unpredictable Order assassin. Dominates combat with rapid weapon swaps, deceptive range, and lethal multi-slash combos.”

weapons.name: Twisted Agony
weapons.note: In-game card: “The eccentric Ghost. Imbued with chaos and relentless strength.”

weapons.name: Thunder Prodigy
weapons.note: Lightning-themed Epic weapon. An early-game option you replace when a Legendary or better drops.

weapons.name: Cosmic Warrior
weapons.note: Epic all-rounder that carries the first dungeons comfortably and stops being exciting by the mid-game.

weapons.name: Rubber Man
weapons.note: In-game card: “The legendary Straw Hat captain. Dominates close combat with fast-paced rubber combos and heavy impact strikes.”

weapons.name: Hu Tao
weapons.note: Shows up in creator videos and one competitor roster, including as an evolution target. No source we checked states its rarity, so it stays unranked here.

weapons.name: Igris
weapons.note: Seen in Shadow Monarch update footage ("max upgraded OP Igris"). No published roster lists its rarity or kit yet.

weapons.name: Sung Jin-Woo
weapons.note: The chase entity of the Shadow Monarch update — creators advertise "0.01% Sung Jin-Woo" pulls. Rarity and mechanics are not documented by any published source.

weapons.name: Dragon Eclipse
weapons.note: In-game card: “The legendary Black Swordsman. Dominates close combat with heavy sweeping attacks and relentless strength.” Writer rosters list this kit as “Guts” after the character it is themed on; the card in the game says Dragon Eclipse, and this site uses the in-game name. S tier on the circulating tier board.

weapons.name: Immortal Sovereign
weapons.note: In-game card: “Marked for death, he defies his fate, cleaving his enemies with pure brute hate!” This is the Shadow Monarch chase entity that update videos advertise as “0.01%” — none of the four competitor rosters names it. A tier on the circulating board.

weapons.name: Divine Emperor
weapons.note: In-game card: “The legendary Divine Emperor. Dominates the battlefield with massive Conqueror's Haki range and heavy blade strikes.” Second Arcane weapon in the game; absent from every competitor roster checked. A tier on the circulating board.

weapons.name: Void Arbiter
weapons.note: The unit the Void Arbiter update (UPD 3) is named after. You don't summon it at the Arsenal. One creator got it by clearing Trials floor 200. In that video the evolve screen asked for 5,000,000 Coins and 50 Magic Pendants, among other items, and the skill tree maxed at level 104. No source states its rarity.

weapons.name: Ye Shunguang
weapons.note: One of the new units from the Void Arbiter update, earned in Trials instead of the Arsenal. The October 13 patch reworked it: a new 6-hit basic combo, a new block animation for both forms, and a fix for skill 3 firing the wrong way. That comes from patch notes read out in a creator video. Rarity and the in-game card name aren't published.

weapons.name: Astra Yao
weapons.note: A support unit from the Void Arbiter update, earned in Trials. Its skill buffs your damage, so creators pair it with a main damage unit. The October 13 patch made that buff stronger and last longer, per patch notes shown in a creator video. Rarity and the in-game card name aren't published.

weapons.name: Crimson Eclipse
weapons.note: The fighter from the Update 4 Tidal High Rise mode, themed after Chisa. Twin blades and giant scissors. You craft it from the mode's drops. Rarity isn't published yet.
weapons.howToGet: You can't summon Crimson Eclipse. Clear Tidal High Rise (Nightmare only), collect the Crimson Eclipse materials it drops, then craft it in the crafting menu. The materials only drop, you can't craft them.
details: Tidal High Rise: climb a flooding tower from the underground parking lot before the water catches you. On each floor you clear enemies, pull the lever and hold the gate, and there's a mini-boss on every floor.
Every gate you hold pays coins and XP even if the run fails. Clearing the roof pays 18,000 coins and 500 gems on top of the Crimson Eclipse materials.
It fights with twin blades and giant scissors.
It has an evolution (Evo). Evolving takes another, bigger batch of the mode's materials, and its ultimate skill unlocks through the skill tree with more drops.
Drops are slow. Creators suggest farming it with a party rather than solo.

weapons.name: Solar Radiance
weapons.note: The fighter from the Update 4 Evil Reflection raid, themed after Cha Hae-In from Solo Leveling. You can't summon it: you craft it from the raid's drops. Rarity isn't published yet.
weapons.howToGet: You can't summon Solar Radiance. Play the Evil Reflection raid (Nightmare only), farm the materials it drops, then craft Solar Radiance in the crafting menu.
details: Evil Reflection is a Nightmare-only raid: four waves of copies of your own avatar using weapons from other maps, then a fifth wave where your evil twin fights with your own gear.
The evil twin calls for help at 60% health and splits apart after taking damage at 50% and 25%.
After each of waves one to four you pick one of three mirror blessings. You get three lives for the whole run.
Its awakened ultimate combines with the Shadow Lord ultimate into one dual ultimate. Creators call it the first combined ultimate in the game.
One creator counts five skills on it, and it plays as a fast skill-spam damage dealer.

systems.name: The Arsenal (Rolls and Lucky Spins)
systems.detail: Weapons are summoned here, not bought. Rolls are the common currency and Lucky Spins are the better-odds one. No official odds or pity numbers are published — any percentage you see online is community guesswork.

systems.name: Traits and rerolls
systems.detail: Traits are modifiers attached to a weapon and Trait Rerolls are the currency that changes them. Rerolls are the resource most worth hoarding — four codes alone pay out hundreds of them.

systems.name: Two weapon slots
systems.detail: You equip two weapons and swap between them mid-dungeon. Community reports two traps: some Zenless weapons refuse a second copy, and summoning while a weapon is equipped can overwrite it together with its trait. Check both slots before you roll.

systems.name: Dungeons and modes
systems.detail: The game runs a story path plus higher-intensity modes — the Shadow Monarch update added a raid, and creators also farm an AFK chamber and Endless-style runs. The Void Arbiter update added Trials, a tower mode: each stage is 5 floors of 2 waves, and the new units drop from it (Void Arbiter itself at floor 200). Creators say the October 13 patch made Trials easier. Each mode has its own recommended level, which none of the reputable listings agree on yet.

systems.name: Evolution and awakening
systems.detail: Weapons evolve along a rarity ladder (Epic → Legendary → Mythic → Arcane → Zenless). Evolution generally wants a duplicate or a specific material — the exact cost per tier is unpublished.

systems.name: Accessories
systems.detail: Crafted from Gems, equipped for passive bonuses. Gems come from codes and dungeon drops, which is why gem codes disappear fast.

systems.name: Titles and quests
systems.detail: Account-level progression with their own rewards. Useful for early levelling because quest XP is free, unlike rerolls.

redeemSteps: Launch Anime Zero on Roblox and wait for your character to load in.
Open the Codes menu — it sits among the buttons on the right side of the HUD.
Paste a code exactly as written. Codes are case-sensitive, so use the copy button instead of retyping.
Press Redeem. If a code is level-gated (50KCCU-tier codes are not, but several need level 25 or 50), redeem it again once you pass the requirement.
